gen-dafont-disorder-noto-serif: Disorder draws hollow glass-tube letters of constant thickness, set well apart, with a rawness that feels deliberately unruly. Noto Serif then settles things with a gentle ebb and flow of weight.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-satoshi: Understated and decorative, Espresso Dolce writes in a calligraphic hand with wide-eyed e's and a thickness like neon glass tubing. Satoshi stays uniform and tall, so pages of it move along without friction.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-switzer: Espresso Dolce is a calligraphic script with wide-eyed lowercase e's. Switzer sits beside it as a tall, wire-like sans-serif, crisp and Swiss where the script is soft and glowing.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-lora: Aggressive and fast, Ethnocentric pushes its letters well apart, with short ascenders sitting above big bowls. Lora lets the page breathe afterward, bookish and gently thinning at the curves.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-noto-serif: Loud and low-slung, Ethnocentric spreads its letters wide over big bowls. Noto Serif follows with a subtle thick-thin cadence and a prominent x-height, thinning slightly at the sides of each bowl.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-cascadia-code: Wide glass portholes and clipped terminals: Existence looks industrial, every letter part carrying the same visual mass. Cascadia Code runs wire-like and monoline, widely spaced, smooth round every bend.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads compact, its letters standing like pins in a wide board. Existence makes its mark with wide glass-porthole counters, while Cascadia Mono holds curves and stems to the same weight.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-peta: Industrial through and through, Existence gives lowercase counters the look of wide glass portholes, terminals cut short. Lexend Peta stands out most: its curves never thin anywhere along the stroke.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta is widely tracked, with tall-bodied small letters. Existence is the louder one, all porthole counters and clipped terminals, while Lexend Zetta cuts its strokes like ribbon at constant width.
gen-dafont-forza-fs-bespoke-serif: Crowded like beads on a wire, Forza hugs its terminals to the bowl. Bespoke Serif then loosens things with thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, dignified against that rod-stock rigidity.
